scope: Minimum core intelligence bundle materialized from the frozen Round 3F-B learning statements supplied by the approved contract; no new research or theory added.

learning_records.observed_problem: All scenes carry equal visual hierarchy, obscuring the customer's current decision.
learning_records.decision_principle: Determine what deserves authority now; make the object the customer must judge now the screen's dominant.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: The current decision target is immediately identifiable as the visual and informational dominant.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Reduces uncertainty about what the visitor should understand at this point.
required_conditions: A customer decision is identified for the scene
The dominant is supported by available evidence
asset_dependency: decision-relevant evidence when the dominant is factual
low_evidence_translation: Use hierarchy and guided choice to give decision authority without fabricated proof
failure_modes: All scenes use the same visual hierarchy
Authority is assigned to unsupported claims
do_not_reuse_when: No current customer decision can be identified

learning_records.observed_problem: Information and immersive context compete for attention.
learning_records.decision_principle: Shift from information to immersion only when the customer's task changes.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: The scene's informational or experiential mode visibly follows the customer's current need.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Supports orientation first and experience when it contributes to understanding.
required_conditions: A meaningful customer-state change exists
Immersion does not conceal required information
asset_dependency: relevant media or intentional spatial context
low_evidence_translation: Adjust information hierarchy and pacing without inventing atmosphere as evidence
failure_modes: Background decoration without a decision role
do_not_reuse_when: The scene remains an information task

learning_records.observed_problem: Proof competes with high-energy or visually noisy surroundings.
learning_records.decision_principle: Quiet the field so proof becomes dominant.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Evidence is easier to locate and read because the surrounding field recedes.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Makes available proof legible without exaggerating its authority.
required_conditions: Real, relevant proof exists
Reduced visual competition preserves its context
low_evidence_translation: When proof is absent, state the evidence boundary; do not manufacture substitute proof
do_not_reuse_when: There is no proof to foreground

learning_records.observed_problem: A page changes backgrounds mechanically at every section.
learning_records.decision_principle: Background continuity can be intentional; background change is not mandatory.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Continuity or transition has a discernible role instead of becoming a repeated section marker.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Preserves coherence and directs attention to meaningful changes.
required_conditions: Continuity supports the page's decision sequence
low_evidence_translation: Use information grouping and pacing; do not add imagery solely to create background variation
do_not_reuse_when: Continuity causes distinct decision states to become indistinguishable

learning_records.observed_problem: Multiple elements compete and no meaningful dominant emerges.
learning_records.decision_principle: Establish one meaningful dominant for each decision moment.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: One evidence-backed task or choice leads; supporting content remains subordinate.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Improves orientation without hiding necessary qualifications.
required_conditions: Scene has one primary customer decision
Supporting information remains accessible
asset_dependency: only when media is the decision-relevant dominant
low_evidence_translation: Use hierarchy, editing, or guided choice when evidence assets are weak
do_not_reuse_when: The scene genuinely requires parallel equal decisions

learning_records.observed_problem: Repeated section rhythm hides a consequential change in customer state.
learning_records.decision_principle: Break repeated rhythm only at a meaningful decision point.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: A consequential choice is perceptibly distinct from routine supporting information.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Signals when the visitor's decision context has changed.
required_conditions: The decision point is material and traceable
low_evidence_translation: Use spacing, information editing, or typographic role rather than fabricated visual proof
failure_modes: Visual break has no customer-decision meaning
do_not_reuse_when: No material decision transition occurs

learning_records.observed_problem: The same spatial grammar persists after the customer's task materially changes.
learning_records.decision_principle: Change spatial grammar when customer state materially changes.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: The composition communicates a real change in what the visitor is doing or deciding.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Helps distinguish exploration, evaluation, and action.
required_conditions: Customer-state transition is supported by strategy
low_evidence_translation: Use guided choice, hierarchy, or information editing without adding unsupported scene claims
do_not_reuse_when: Customer state is unchanged

learning_records.observed_problem: Asset authority is weak, so visual authority risks being faked.
learning_records.decision_principle: When asset authority is weak, increase decision authority instead of inventing evidence.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: The visitor can still understand distinctions and next decisions without false proof cues.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Maintains clarity and trust while making evidence limits visible.
required_conditions: Unknowns remain explicitly bounded
Decision task can be supported with verified facts
low_evidence_translation: hierarchy
process clarity only when process is verified
guided choice
information editing
background pacing
meaningful typography
CTA architecture
late-page resolution
failure_modes: Generated staff, reviews, process, premises, or metrics presented as fact
do_not_reuse_when: A proposed translation implies unsupported factual evidence

learning_records.observed_problem: Stock or generated media appears without helping the customer decide.
learning_records.decision_principle: Assign media an explicit role: EVIDENCE, DESIRE, CONTEXT, PROCESS, EMOTION, or IDENTIFICATION.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Each media item has an understandable decision-support role and is not mistaken for proof outside that role.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Connects visual attention to a customer need while protecting evidence integrity.
required_conditions: Media role is declared
Actual evidence is not confused with representative imagery
low_evidence_translation: Omit media if its role cannot be supported; use verified text or structure instead
failure_modes: Representative image presented as actual evidence
do_not_reuse_when: No safe, meaningful media role exists

learning_records.observed_problem: Expressive typography dominates scenes that require calm evaluation.
learning_records.decision_principle: Expressive typography should not dominate every scene.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Type emphasis varies with scene purpose; informational scenes remain readable and credible.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Balances attention with comprehension.
required_conditions: Typography hierarchy follows customer task
Responsive legibility is preserved
low_evidence_translation: Use meaningful hierarchy and restrained emphasis without treating scale as proof
failure_modes: Uniform expressive display across all scenes
do_not_reuse_when: Expressive type itself is necessary to communicate the specific offer

learning_records.observed_problem: Conditions and proof are visually subordinate to promotional copy.
learning_records.decision_principle: Quiet typography can carry trust, conditions, and proof.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Supporting facts and limitations are legible without competing as headlines.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Allows informed evaluation and expectation setting.
required_conditions: The supporting fact is verified
Text remains readable on target viewports
low_evidence_translation: Use typographic clarity for known facts and explicit unknown boundaries
do_not_reuse_when: Quiet treatment makes essential information inaccessible

learning_records.observed_problem: One typographic voice is applied regardless of scene purpose.
learning_records.decision_principle: Typography role should vary by scene purpose.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Orientation, proof, explanation, and action have distinguishable reading roles.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Supports scanning and comprehension across decision stages.
required_conditions: Scene purposes are specified
No role impairs Japanese readability
low_evidence_translation: Vary hierarchy and role, not unsupported authority claims
do_not_reuse_when: Role variation introduces inconsistent or inaccessible reading

learning_records.observed_problem: Content after the hero becomes information storage instead of continuing to resolve decisions.
learning_records.decision_principle: Late-page content continues resolving customer decisions.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Each late scene answers a remaining question or supports the next decision.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Maintains decision continuity toward contact without assuming conversion lift.
required_conditions: Remaining customer questions are grounded in truth/evidence
Information is relevant to the conversion path
low_evidence_translation: Edit, reorder, and qualify verified information; preserve unknowns
failure_modes: Late sections disconnected from customer tension
do_not_reuse_when: No verified information exists for the proposed answer

learning_records.observed_problem: The page continues selling desire after the visitor needs proof or risk resolution.
learning_records.decision_principle: Authority can shift from desire to proof and risk resolution.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Later content prioritizes the visitor's remaining proof or risk question over repeated desire cues.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Supports informed readiness to act.
required_conditions: Relevant proof or risk information is verified
Unknowns are not filled with fabricated reassurance
asset_dependency: verified proof only when proof is presented
low_evidence_translation: State what is known, what is unknown, and how to contact the business
failure_modes: Hero-like selling repeated through the page
do_not_reuse_when: No verified proof exists to answer the proposed question

learning_records.observed_problem: FAQ or a boxed CTA is treated as mandatory regardless of customer need.
learning_records.decision_principle: FAQ and CTA boxes are not mandatory; use them only when they resolve a real decision or action need.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Late-page components appear only when their content and form serve the customer's remaining decision.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Avoids formulaic friction and irrelevant repetition.
required_conditions: A real unresolved question or action need exists
low_evidence_translation: Use a direct verified contact path without inventing FAQs
do_not_reuse_when: The component adds no new decision information

learning_records.observed_problem: The ending uses a standard CTA box without acknowledging the visitor's remaining decision.
learning_records.decision_principle: End around the customer's remaining decision; a final CTA box is not the default answer.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: The ending resolves or acknowledges the visitor's actual remaining question and presents a fitting verified next action.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Makes action contextually coherent without claiming improved conversion.
required_conditions: Remaining decision is known from strategy
CTA destination is verified
low_evidence_translation: Use the verified @happyfuture_02 route and invite a service-specific question without asserting unverified details
do_not_reuse_when: The proposed ending assumes a decision state not supported by strategy

learning_records.observed_problem: Desktop layout is merely stacked on mobile, changing the intended decision hierarchy.
learning_records.decision_principle: Mobile keeps the same thesis but uses a different composition; reorder by decision priority.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: The same customer decision remains clear through a mobile-specific information order.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Preserves comprehension and action path on mobile.
required_conditions: Mobile decision priority is explicit
No required fact or choice is hidden
low_evidence_translation: Reorder verified information for mobile instead of shrinking desktop composition
do_not_reuse_when: Reordering breaks factual or process sequence

learning_records.observed_problem: Responsive changes reduce media to a decorative thumbnail and alter its decision role.
learning_records.decision_principle: Preserve media authority on mobile when media carries a required decision role.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: Media remains legible and appropriately prominent for its declared role on mobile.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Maintains context or evidence needed for understanding.
required_conditions: Media role is valid and safe
Mobile crop preserves relevant context
low_evidence_translation: Do not enlarge weak or unverified media; use structure or text if safe media is unavailable
failure_modes: Media reduced to an unexplained thumbnail
do_not_reuse_when: Media has no valid decision role

learning_records.observed_problem: Mobile removes the resolution meaning established by the ending.
learning_records.decision_principle: Preserve ending meaning on mobile, not necessarily desktop form.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: The visitor's remaining decision and verified next action remain coherent at mobile width.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Preserves action context across viewport change.
required_conditions: Ending meaning and verified CTA are identified
low_evidence_translation: Retain the remaining-decision copy and verified route using a mobile-appropriate composition
failure_modes: Desktop CTA reduced to a generic mobile button
do_not_reuse_when: The desktop ending itself is not strategy-grounded

learning_records.observed_problem: Agency signature or generic premium conventions dominate business reality.
learning_records.decision_principle: Derive design from business structure, customer tension, offer, proof, and conversion reality.
learning_records.human_visible_effect: The experience reflects this business's actual service distinctions, customer decision, evidence boundary, and verified contact route.
learning_records.persuasion_effect: Improves relevance and truthfulness; performance impact remains unproven.
required_conditions: Business truth is frozen and traceable
Proof and conversion facts are verified
asset_dependency: only assets with a declared and supported role
low_evidence_translation: Use verified service structure, location, and contact; do not fill gaps with generic premium styling or fabricated proof
failure_modes: Company name can be swapped without changing decision logic
do_not_reuse_when: Truth boundary is missing or contaminated
